Ricardo! I have news from Dubrovnik. The city council made new rules for the old town.
Really? After all those crowds in August? What are the new rules?
First, you mustn't walk in the streets in your swimsuit. If you do, you get a fine.
That makes sense. The old town is not a beach. And the old buildings?
You mustn't sit on the fountain or on the church steps. Visitors have to respect the monuments.
And do I have to book a time to enter, like at a museum?
No, you don't have to. Only big tour groups have to book, and their guides must have a permit.
So the city didn't ban tourists. It asked them to behave. And what about you? What do the people who live there think?
Most of us are happy. We have to live here every day, after all. Are you allowed to sit on monuments in Sao Paulo?
Officially, no. But not everybody follows that rule!

Good morning, everybody, and welcome to the old town. Before we walk through the gate, I have to tell you about a few rules, because the city is very strict now. First, you mustn't walk in the streets in your swimsuit. The beach is beautiful, but the old town is not a beach, and the police can give you a fine. Second, please don't sit on the steps of the churches or on the fountain. They are monuments, and they are more than five hundred years old. You don't have to be silent, of course, but people live here, so please respect their homes. And one more thing. Our group has a booked time, so we have to be back at this gate at twelve o'clock. If you can't find us, call me. Shall we go in?

I am on the city council, and I want to explain our new rules, because some people say that we hate tourists. That is not true. Visitors are welcome here. But last summer, on some days, there were more visitors than residents in the old town. Families moved out, and the little shops which sold bread became souvenir shops. So now big tour groups have to book a time to enter, and only two cruise ships can stop here each day. Visitors don't have to pay to walk in the old town. It is still free. We simply ask them to respect the city. A city is not a museum. People must be able to live in it.

First Elena called Ricardo with news from the city council. Then she said that visitors mustn't walk in the streets in their swimsuits. After that she explained that they have to respect the monuments. Then Ricardo asked if he had to book a time, and Elena said: No, you don't have to. In the end they talked about the rules in Sao Paulo.
